title: Unit 1 Practice Test 4: Polynomial Functions
subtitle: 5 Questions -- 11 Points
purpose: Short targeted drill built from cross-assessment weakness analysis across 3 unit tests (Unit Exam 68%D, PT2 86%B, PT3). Primary targets: divide-factor-graph synthesis, find ALL zeros including complex, sign accuracy on factoring, exponent rules with distribution and combining like terms.

questions.targets: Synthesis: divide with given factor, factor result, find zeros with multiplicities, sketch graph
questions.question_html: Given $f(x) = x^3 - 3x + 2$ and that $(x + 2)$ is a factor: (a) Divide out $(x + 2)$ and factor the result completely. (b) Find all zeros and state the multiplicity of each. (c) Sketch the graph. Label the zeros and show correct end behavior.

a.division: Divide x^3 - 3x + 2 by (x+2): quotient is x^2 - 2x + 1

key_visual: crosses x-axis at x=-2 going up
bounces at x=1 (touches and falls back)

answer_key.scoring_rubric: 1 pt: correct division and fully factored form. 1 pt: both zeros with correct multiplicities. 1 pt: sketch with correct end behavior and bounce vs cross at each zero.

graph_spec.render_instructions: Student sketches on blank axes. Provide empty coordinate grid with x-axis from -4 to 4.

questions.targets: PERSISTENT: stop-after-first-zero pattern. Irrational remaining roots from dividing out one real zero.
questions.question_html: Find ALL zeros of $f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 4x + 12$. The table shows $f(3) = 0$. Show your division work.
questions.note: Table also shows f(2)=0 -- student may use either. Both (x-3) and (x-2) are factors. Third zero is x=-2.

answer_key.scoring_rubric: 1 pt: divide correctly and get x^2 - 4. 1 pt: all three zeros correct.
answer_key.coaching_tip: After finding one zero from the table, divide it out. The quotient is a quadratic you can factor. A cubic always has 3 zeros.

questions.targets: RECURRING: sign error on factor-to-zero + negative GCF
questions.question_html: Factor $f(x) = -2x^3 + 8x^2 + 10x$ completely. Then find ALL zeros.

answer_key.scoring_rubric: 1 pt: factored completely with -2x as GCF. 1 pt: all three zeros correct with correct signs.
answer_key.coaching_tip: (x-5)=0 means x=+5. (x+1)=0 means x=-1. The zero is always the opposite sign of what is in the parentheses.

questions.targets: NEW: exponent rules -- distribute into binomial, multiply monomials (add exponents), combine like terms

answer_key.scoring_rubric: 1 pt: correct distribution and monomial multiplication (exponents added correctly). 1 pt: correct final answer after combining like terms.
answer_key.coaching_tip: Step 1: distribute and multiply every product (add exponents). Step 2: collect all terms with the same degree and combine coefficients.

questions.targets: PERSISTENT: stop-after-visible-zeros pattern. Degree 4 with 2 real + 2 complex zeros.
questions.question_html: Find ALL zeros of $f(x) = x^4 - x^3 + 2x^2 - 4x - 8$. The graph shows the function crosses the x-axis at $x = -1$ and $x = 2$. Show your division work.

graph_spec.render_instructions: Graph provided on test. Smooth curve, both ends up, crosses at x=-1 and x=2. No equation shown. Dots on both real zeros.

worked_solution: x=-1 and x=2 given from graph
answer_key.scoring_rubric: 1 pt: divide out both real zeros correctly and arrive at x^2+4. 1 pt: x=+/-2i with correct i notation.
answer_key.coaching_tip: Degree 4 means 4 total zeros. The graph only shows 2. Divide out both real zeros and solve what remains. x^2+4=0 has no real solutions -- the answer involves i.
